title: Check new submissions after a worker failure, not only failed futures
applies_when: An asynchronous compiler or other optional process pool promises an in-process fallback when background execution is unavailable.
lesson: Trace two distinct failure transitions: an already-submitted future fails, and a subsequent new key is submitted to the now-broken executor. Handling future.result() alone does not cover executor.submit() raising before a future exists. Test an actual terminated worker, then a new submission through the real caller. Verify failed submission does not reserve the key or increment successful-submission counters, the intended fallback returns correct values, and exceptions from the fallback itself still propagate. Keep submission recovery separate from computation-error handling.
avoid_when: Do not silently switch to local execution when distributed execution is required for correctness, isolation or resources. Do not swallow arbitrary programming errors or infer that a broken executor has recovered. An explicit shutdown may be an application lifecycle error rather than a supported fallback. A CPU compile stand-in validates host control flow, not CUDA compilation, numerical kernel correctness or performance.

evidence.note: The actual cold-cache caller defers only when submit returns True; False reaches the existing in-process path. Polling failed futures and submitting a new key are separate transitions.

Repository-native CPU regressions use real shut-down and abruptly terminated process pools. Six cases fail with the submission fix removed and pass after it, including actual jit_cache control flow with a CPU compile stand-in and propagation of its own error. GPU-dependent tests were not executed; this evidence is not a kernel performance result.
Open contribution containing the scoped fix and reproduction details; publication does not establish maintainer acceptance or merge.
